newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 29.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Tuesday:
- The death of the key banker in the 40 million Ansbacher Deposits affair will seriously hinder new investigations into the so-called finance of Charles Haughey and the so-called "golden circle".
- A last-ditch attempt to save the U2 concerts planned for Lansdowne Road is to be made by the promoters and the Irish Rugby Football Union.
- The government has set October 30 as the date for the presidential election.
- The government has just nine months to save EU funding worth 92 million for Dublin's proposed light rail system.
- The British Army and RUC security measures in the North are being wound down in the wake of the IRA ceasefire.
- The government is expected to re-invite tenders for the national convention centre, reversing an earlier decision approving an application from the RDS.
- The McCole family has made a dramatic eleventh hour appeal to the government not to publish the state's legal strategy in their late mother's case.
- Any new inquiry into the finances of Charles Haughey has lost one of its most important potential witnesses with the death of the Cayman Island banker John Furze.
THE EXAMINER - U2 still haven't found what they're looking for - a venue for the Irish leg of their PopMart world tour.
- The Catholic Church is expected to legally defend all civil
actions taken against it by victims of paedophile priest Brendan Smyth.
- Hopes of solving the mystery surrounding the 40 million Ansbacher accounts at the centre of the payments to politicians tribunal have been dashed by the death of a key figure in the controversy.
